summary: Repaired writer.py on node1. It now reopens audit.log on SIGHUP, releases the deleted file descriptor, continues writing without restarting, and closes cleanly on SIGTERM. Ubuntu 7.10 and kernel 2.6.22-14-generic were retained. Restart persistence was verified.
actions_performed: Added Python 2.5-compatible SIGHUP and SIGTERM handlers.
Verified recovery after unlinking audit.log using the same process.
Verified clean SIGTERM shutdown with no traceback or subsequent writes.
Preserved the A100 archive record and A101 current record.
Safely restarted node1 and verified the changed boot identity, SSH recovery, files, data, and writer execution.

evidence.requirement: SIGHUP reopens the current audit.log, releases the deleted descriptor, and continues without process restart
evidence.summary: PID 4694 initially held audit.log; after unlink it showed a deleted descriptor. Following SIGHUP, the same PID used the new inode, had no deleted descriptor, and the line count continued increasing.

evidence.requirement: SIGTERM closes the log and exits cleanly
evidence.summary: The writer exited promptly, produced no traceback, and audit.log stopped growing.
archive/previous.log retained record A100 and SHA-1 5355b97cc10231092b2bf7bc7c31d12f66508a8d throughout testing and restart.

evidence.requirement: Repair is compatible with the installed legacy platform
evidence.summary: The repair compiles under Python 2.5.1; Ubuntu 7.10 and kernel 2.6.22-14-generic remained installed.

Healthy baseline used boot ID 74867a28-27cc-44d8-8efe-8cd682716564; reboot was acknowledged; node1 returned with boot ID acf0a705-e79c-4bef-aed3-f96af2bba627. SSH, source syntax/mode, audit records, archive checksum, writer output, and clean termination were verified after restart.
